items.claim: The unit MT 33:1-33:9 stands, but the reason given against the rival cut is false on the bytes. That rival seam is said to have no fresh formula onset at MT 33:7, and MT 33:7 does carry the son-of-man address - 1 of the book's 93 such verses - in the very skeleton that opens MT 33:10, MT 33:12 and MT 33:30, with a setumah standing immediately before it after MT 33:6. The row's own device note names the MT 33:7 address, so the two halves of this row disagree and the device note is the true half.
items.both_sides: Kept seam, MT 33:9/33:10 - close side: a setumah follows MT 33:9 and the verse belongs to neither refrain set, so nothing formulaic closes it; onset side: MT 33:10 carries וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם and a quoted popular saying, a fresh subject. Rival seam, MT 33:6/33:7 - close side: a setumah follows MT 33:6, which likewise carries no refrain; onset side: MT 33:7 carries וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם, the same address, differing from MT 33:10 only in its accents. The two seams are therefore of equal grade in both mark and onset device, and what separates them is subject, not form: MT 33:7-33:9 keeps the watchman figure and turns it on the prophet, while MT 33:10 leaves the figure for the people's despair. That is the ground the rejection needs.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 33:7 carries the son-of-man address, 1 of the book's 93, in the same skeleton as MT 33:10, with a setumah before it after MT 33:6; the rival cut is declined on continuity of subject, not on an absent onset device

items.claim: Two textual-variant sites inside this span are undisclosed, and one punctuation fact is asserted beyond what the witness can show. MT 33:13 and MT 33:16 are each a ketiv/qere site; the span covers both and the row records neither, although the neighbouring unit expressly denies that class for its own span. Separately the row asserts that MT 33:20 carries no sof-pasuq in this witness: the extract carries no sof-pasuq glyph at any of the book's 1,273 verses and the parashah record holds no per-verse entry for that glyph, so no verse's sof-pasuq can be read either way from the pinned material.
items.both_sides: The span itself is right, and for a firmer reason than the row gives. The rival seam inside it is MT 33:11/33:12 - close side: MT 33:11 carries the utterance refrain נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה and a petuchah follows the verse, the only open-section division inside MT 33:1-33:20 apart from the one after MT 33:20; onset side: MT 33:12 carries וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם, the same address that opens MT 33:10, with the addressee moving from the house of Israel to the children of your people. What defeats that seam is position: the refrain in MT 33:11 is not verse-final and its accents say so - revia U+0597 on the divine name, where the verse-final occurrences at MT 34:15, MT 34:30 and MT 34:31 carry meteg U+05BD - so the close-grade limb of the seam test is not met, and MT 33:11 ends instead on the appeal to the house of Israel. The row reaches the same conclusion from content alone; the accents settle it.

items.claim: Every Masoretic and formula fact this row asserts is true on the bytes, and its seam reading is corroborated by the accents beyond what it claims: MT 34:1 carries the strict-form word-event onset with a setumah behind it after MT 33:33; the messenger formula stands at MT 34:2, MT 34:10 and MT 34:11; the utterance refrain stands at MT 34:8 and MT 34:15; the interior setumahs after MT 34:8 and after MT 34:10 are both disclosed; and MT 34:16 belongs to no formula set and carries no paragraph mark, exactly as stated.
items.both_sides: Close side, MT 34:15 and MT 34:16: the refrain נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה stands verse-final at MT 34:15, which its accents confirm - meteg U+05BD on the divine name - and MT 34:16 adds no formula and no mark. Onset side, MT 34:17: the messenger formula stands behind וְאַתֵּ֣נָה צֹאנִ֔י, a second-feminine-plural addressee replacing the third-person description of the shepherds. No paragraph mark falls at this seam, and the row does not claim one. The nearest marked division, the setumah after MT 34:10, opens on כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה at MT 34:11, whose subordinating connective binds the clause to what precedes it; and the refrain at MT 34:8 is mid-verse, revia U+0597 on the divine name rather than the verse-final cadence, so neither mark is a close. Reading both as internal is what the accents support.

triage_answers.both_sides: The seam test this entry rests on requires a refrain-grade close followed by a sub-onset. Within this cluster that test is now testable on the accents, which is the contribution offered: the utterance refrain is verse-final at MT 34:15, MT 34:30 and MT 34:31, where it carries meteg U+05BD on the divine name, and mid-verse at MT 33:11 and MT 34:8, where it carries revia U+0597. On the entry's own quoted bytes the refrain at MT 21:18 (= WEB 21:13) carries the verse-final cadence, meteg U+05BD, so the close-grade limb of the test is met there, unlike at MT 33:11. Numbering identity holds in chapters 33 and 34; the dual is given for the chapter-21 reference because it falls in the numbering zone. Whether the sword figure's continuity outweighs that turns on verses outside this cluster and is left where it belongs.
